content.title: How Michigan crushed Arizona in men’s Final Four to reach NCAA Tournament national title game
content.text: The Wolverines dominated the Wildcats 91-73 in the national semifinals and will face UConn for the championshipMichigan will be seeking its second national title on Monday. Getty ImagesWolverines destroy WildcatsMichigan dominated Arizona in the men’s Final Four, winning 91-73 tonight to advance to the NCAA Tournament championship game.The Wolverines will face UConn on Monday night for the title. Michigan will be seeking its second championship in program history (1989).Aday Mara led a balanced Michigan attack with 26 points, while Trey McKenney came off the bench to score 16. Five Michigan players scored in double figures, and Elliot Cadeau had a double-double with 13 points and 10 assists. Share your thoughts on the games: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMonday night's odds Getty ImagesBoth Michigan and UConn got off to hot starts in Saturday’s Final Four games. The Huskies had to endure a push from Illinois while the Wolverines ran away from Arizona. Considering Michigan’s dominant play, it’s no surprise the Wolverines are big favorites for Monday’s national championship game.Michigan is favored by 7.5 points on DraftKings, BetMGM and FanDuel. The Wolverines opened as a 6.5-point favorite on FanDuel, but that number quickly moved so that all three sportsbooks showed matching odds.May praises Mara Imagn ImagesDusty May on Aday Mara (26 points, nine rebounds and three assists): 💬 “Aday was sensational.”“He was at the rim, catching lobs. He was a force down low. He was a pressure release up top. I mean, he’s such a smart basketball player, and obviously, his rim protection, he did a great job on (Koa) Peat. He did a great job forcing a lot of those misses around the basket because of his aggression.”Trey McKenney on Michigan’s hot start: 💬 “During the season we have had like some type of mental lapses during big games, but I think we came out, and we really knew how high the stakes were, and we just really wanted to leave it all on the floor. We had nothing left.“Really, we only have a couple of days left with the bonds that we’ve made throughout the summer.”Michigan transfer stars heap praise on coaching staff Imagn ImagesElliot Cadeau (UNC transfer) and Aday Mara (UCLA transfer) spoke to how Dusty May and the Michigan coaching staff integrated a team of four transfers (this season) in a short period of time:Cadeau: 💬 “I think they did a really good job putting four transfers, or five players on the court at all times that are really good at passing the ball. I think they knew that when they were recruiting all of us, just having five people on the court that are all playmakers and also great scorers just helps us have connectivity on the court, for sure.”Mara: 💬 “I think the same. They did a great job putting, as he said, players that were not selfish. And I think now in the era we are with the transfer portal, we’ve just got to learn and adapt as soon as possible to what we have and the different teams that we play. So I think just we’ve got to change and we’ve got to learn every day so we can play together.”Lloyd to TucsonTommy Lloyd’s message to Tucson: “We all saw what’s possible again. So now let’s all roll up our sleeves and support each other and see if we can make this a normal thing.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementCadeau on dome shooting issues Imagn ImagesAdd Elliot Cadeau to the depth perception discussion of basketball games in football stadiums:💬 “I think it kind of takes a little time to get used to shooting at game speed in this arena.”Don't count out UConnTommy Lloyd on people saying tonight’s Michigan-Arizona matchup was a de facto championship game: “Listen, I don’t think anybody is going to count UConn out. So that’s why when everybody was saying this is the national championship game, it’s not the national championship game. Monday night is the national championship game, and you have to fight to get there. So, yeah, credit to Michigan. Really impressive tonight.” Imagn ImagesDusty May on Yaxel Lendeborg returning to finish tonight's Final Four game: 💬 “The guys know that Yax is about winning.”A big takeaway from tonight’s game is the sheer importance of experience, particularly in March. Tommy Lloyd was asked about that, given the lack of experience from his Arizona stars.💬 “I don’t think it was inexperience today. We had a good couple of days of practice. We had a good shoot-around today. I think we just came out, and we played a team that was really well built. They have a great coach. They were able to take control of the game, and then really, they were like surgical at a point.”Lendeborg draws praise from his teammates Imagn ImagesYaxel Lendeborg was going to return to play in the second half of the game despite his MCL sprain and ankle sprain. He turned to his family and friends during the game to say so, yelling, “I have to, I have to.” He confirmed to CBS Sports’ Tracy Wolfson that he’s going to play in Monday’s national championship game against UConn no matter what: “I’m going to play unless I can’t walk at all.”His teammates, Elliot Cadeau and Trey McKenney, sang their star forward praises for his resilience.Cadeau: 💬 “We know what type of guy Yaxel is, if he can play, he’s going to play. We asked him, ‘Are you good?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ So we expect him to be on the court. He told us when he got on the court, he was going to give it his all.”McKenney: 💬 “I think it just shows the guy who Yaxel is. I mean, he just wants to put it all on the floor for Michigan, and he wants to give the fans what they came here for. I’m just really grateful to have him as a teammate. He’s one of the best players in the country. He really showed that tonight. But he’s selfless as well. So I’m just really grateful to be around him.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementCredit to LloydGot to credit Tommy Lloyd for the way he’s handled this loss. Speaking to Tracy Wolfson immediately after an 18-point loss in the Final Four, Lloyd gave Michigan all the credit and took accountability.At his postgame news conference, Lloyd said: “Michigan gets all the credit today.”He added: “It wasn’t our night, probably had a lot to do with them. They were just impressive. They were impressive how they came out and executed their game plan. And we got down a little bit, and we’ve been down a few times this year, but not like that. Just probably got a little panicky and weren’t able to settle back in. And they get credit. That’s why if you can get off to a good start in games, you know, it’s usually pretty impactful. That definitely was the case today.”Strong 3-point shooting a common theme Getty ImagesDespite playing in Lucas Oil Stadium, UConn and Michigan used 3-point shooting to build insurmountable leads in their respective semifinal victories.Both teams tallied 12 3-pointers in their respective wins, with the Huskies' total setting a new program record for an NCAA Tournament game. UConn accomplished the feat in 33 attempts, while Michigan took only 27 attempts to reach a dozen treys.Keep an eye on long-range attempts from Michigan's Trey McKenney, Elliot Cadeau and Yaxel Lendeborg and UConn's Braylon Mullens and Solo Ball, each who recorded at least three 3-point makes today.Bradley on his time at ArizonaSenior point guard Jaden Bradley on what his three years at Arizona (he was at Alabama his freshman year) meant to him:💬 “It means a lot. I appreciate Coach Lloyd and the staff for taking me in and giving me, I’d like to say, like a fresh start. I appreciate this team. We accomplished a lot this year. We definitely wanted to win this game, but Michigan was a better team tonight. Appreciate Tucson. Just love this group. Cherish the last couple gatherings we have together before everybody goes their own ways, but just happy to be a part of this team.”May: Michigan's performance reflected its identity Getty ImagesMichigan head coach Dusty May’s opening statement after his Wolverines throttled Arizona 91-73, equalling the largest men’s NCAA Tournament win between two No. 1 seeds:💬 “This game was very indicative of how this group has played throughout the season, unselfish basketball. A connected group who defends, gets out in transition and then shares the basketball.“I thought our assist-to-turnover ratio, I thought our job on the glass, especially before the game was not in doubt and is as impressive as anything and but the one thing that we thought really jumped out was our ability to get 50/50 basketballs and be quicker to the ball than Arizona tonight, but just very proud of our effort. What a great group.”Lloyd on Arizona's loss Getty Images Tommy Lloyd’s opening statement after a season-ending defeat to Michigan in the Final Four:💬 “First off, I want to thank the players on our team and the staff. They were amazing this year, and it was an awesome, awesome journey. It was as much fun as I’ve ever had coaching basketball.“Secondly, I want to give credit to Michigan. I mean, they were outstanding tonight. Really had us on our heels tonight. We never could get in a rhythm. So they get a ton of credit for that. No one’s been able to do that to us all year. So it was an impressive performance by them.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMcKenney lights it up Getty ImagesWith Yaxel Lendeborg limited and Elliot Cadeau cold from the field, Trey McKenney stepped up as a human sparkplug for Michigan off the bench. McKenney had the hot hand, going 6-for-9 from the field and 4-for-6 from 3-point range. His 16 points were second on the team, to only Aday Mara's 26.More on Mara Imagn ImagesDusty May says he and the Michigan staff watched Aday Mara's Spanish national team tape and Zaragoza tape as much as his UCLA tape when evaluating him out of the transfer portal last summer:💬 “He had shown glimpses of this. ... But he's playing ball at a high level, and he's adding a lot to our program.” Lindsay Schnell / The AthleticYaxel hasn't had an MRI yet. He said the trainers told him it's likely an MCL sprain. He plans to get an MRI later tonight or tomorrow.First look at Monday nightThe stage is set. UConn and Michigan will play for the national championship in men’s basketball on Monday night in Indianapolis.The No. 2-seeded Huskies, seeking a third title in four seasons, dispatched No. seed 3 Illinois 71-62. Top-seeded Michigan routed fellow No. 1 Arizona 91-73, adding a fourth blowout win to its five-game run through this NCAA Tournament.The results on Saturday ensured a historic result in the title game. No program has won three championships in four years since John Wooden’s UCLA teams more than years ago. And it’s been longer than a quarter-century since a Big Ten team — Michigan State in 2000 — hoisted the trophy.
